target_customer: Small and midsize exporters and importers, first Indian exporters selling to US buyers
problem: Small exporters struggle to get working capital against overseas receivables because banks reject many trade finance applications.
business_model: Trade finance and invoice factoring, fees and interest on advances, funded by equity, bank debt and capital partners

founders.name: Pushkar Mukewar
founders.background_notes: YC page lists no education or prior employers. A search snippet describes a co-founder Neil Kothari but no company source or YC page names him, so he is not listed. Co-founder Neil Kothari added after audit; see his entry.

founders.name: Neil Kothari
founders.background_notes: Wharton MBA classmate and former roommate of Pushkar Mukewar (both WG11) per Wharton Magazine (Spring/Summer 2020); called co-founder and co-CEO by a 2019 Trusted Insight profile. A Village profile lists him as co-CEO until 2021 and board member after; that is a single aggregator.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed underwriting models for foreign buyers, payment collection across borders and bank funding relationships, harder in operations and credit than in software.

defensibility.rationale: Credit performance data and lender relationships build up slowly, but factoring itself was not new and other lenders could copy the model.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Banks retreated from small exporter lending after 2018 according to 2018 coverage, and none absorbed the wedge; no acquisition of Drip was found.

market_need_then: A June 2018 report says small firms make about 40 percent of Indian exports yet face roughly 50 percent rejection rates from banks for trade finance, and banks cut cross-border lending after the PNB scam.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain B2B finance voice in press releases

brand_strength.rationale: No source shows brand pull; name shares words with unrelated Drip email software and growth came from capital partners and sales.

outcome_analysis: Drip Capital kept raising after YC, from a small seed through Series A, B and C plus bank debt, and by 2026 reports more than 9 billion dollars of trade facilitated. Bank pullback from small exporter credit helped, and a 2023 layoff of about 20 percent of staff shows growing pains rather than failure.
notes: Founded year conflicts: YC page says 2016, search results say 2014 to 2016, so null. Company site returned only a loading placeholder. Series A is also reported as 20M including earlier money by YourStory, and the lead is Sequoia in one outlet and Accel in another. Series C 175M is reported as 40M equity plus 135M debt by one aggregator. Totals differ: CB Insights about 508M, Inc42 about 458M. Company blog Series B URL returned 404. A 23M round in Sept 2024 appears only in one aggregator and is unverified. The directory shows Active. Audit fix: the 175M October 2021 announcement (PR Newswire) is split into a 40M Series C equity round and 135M of warehouse debt (a 100M Barclays facility and a 35M East West Bank increase). The earlier note that the split came from one aggregator is superseded. The seed of 120K from Y Combinator dated 2015-08-18 (Xconomy, S15 batch) is added; the separate 5M seed dated 2017 from YourStory conflicts with it and with other outlets, so that figure and date are unresolved (Multiples.vc lists 100K in August 2015, StartupIntros a 2M seed in July 2015). The September 2024 coverage (DealStreetAsia) reports 23M of equity from GMO Payment Gateway and SMBC plus 90M of debt led by IFC and East West Bank, which replaces the earlier note that a 23M round was unverified; it rests on that outlet, with the stage unlabeled. Totals: the press cites about 525M of equity and debt after 2021 and about 640M after 2024; CB Insights about 508M and Inc42 about 458M, which predate or exclude debt, so totals remain approximate and coverage stays partial. Neil Kothari is added as co-founder and co-CEO per Wharton Magazine and Trusted Insight (Entrepreneur India was not opened).
